title: Suricatoos — Fleet Node Enrollment and Renewal
description: Identity lifecycle of a fleet node (ADR-0011). POST /fleet/v1/enroll: the node presents a single-use hub token ('ft_<id>.<secret>', opaque as in ADR-0004) plus a CSR whose CN is its node_id, over TLS that authenticates the HUB (no client certificate yet); the hub answers with a certificate CN=<node_id>, O=<org>, OU=fleet-node issued by the FLEET CA — a trust domain separate from the scanner's enrollment CA — the fleet CA certificate and the Ed25519 command public key. Three pins come out-of-band with the token and are all mandatory: FLEET_HUB_PIN (SPKI of the hub's TLS server certificate or of a CA in its chain) is checked on EVERY handshake, enroll included — client networks may run an interception CA; the node refuses the enroll response unless sha256(fleet CA DER) == FLEET_CA_PIN and sha256(command key SPKI DER) == FLEET_COMMAND_KEY_PIN, then pins both. The node announces schema_versions (MAJOR.MINOR) in the enroll and renew requests, the hub in the enroll/renew response (and both in every heartbeat); enroll and renew go out in the node's HIGHEST version, and a hub that does not support it answers 426 with fleet-heartbeat.schema.json#/$defs/version_unsupported (the token is not consumed) so the node retries in the highest common version. POST /fleet/v1/renew: authenticated by the CURRENT node certificate (mTLS); the CSR must keep CN == node_id; the response has the same shape; the node installs the new certificate ONLY if command_pubkey equals the pinned one and ca_cert equals the pinned fleet CA — otherwise it keeps the current certificate, refuses the response and audits it (no rotation in v1). After the certificate expires, re-enrolling the SAME node_id needs a token the hub bound to that node_id (else 409); the local store is reused and the pins are re-applied from the environment. The root accepts any of the three messages; implementations validate the specific $defs entry.

token.description: single-use, short-TTL hub token; the node discards it after a successful enroll and never logs it

node_id.description: FLEET_NODE_ID, or 'node-' + a UUIDv4 generated and persisted on first boot; must equal the CSR CN
cross-check only: identity comes from the presented certificate (CN)

schema_versions.description: versions the NODE supports (may have changed since the enroll, after an upgrade)

certificate.description: CN=<node_id>, O=<org>, OU=fleet-node; issued by the fleet CA; short TTL (30 days recommended)

ca_cert.description: the fleet CA certificate (checked against FLEET_CA_PIN at enroll)

command_pubkey.description: Ed25519 command verification key, PKIX PEM (checked against FLEET_COMMAND_KEY_PIN at enroll; must stay identical at renew)

csr_pem.description: PKCS#10 PEM; key generated on the node (Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256), private key never leaves it (0600 in FLEET_STATE_DIR)
